subject: Capacity tilt & fallback plan for VerityCare regulated pilot
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@veritycare.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: procurement@veritycare.com
Date: 2028-02-27T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sizing ask: VerityCare pilot hosting options

Marissa / Redwood team,

We’re starting scoping for a 3-month pilot (patient-facing document summarization + embeddings for search) and need to choose hosting posture early. Compliance requires strong isolation and KMS-managed keys. Can you outline recommended committed capacity (GPU counts/types) for both a Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved pool in our VPC) and a Private on-prem model, with a short fallback plan if we need to burst?

Highlights:
- Pilot target: ~15k queries/day, 95th pct latency target ~250ms for short prompts, average response length ~150 tokens.
- Must be HIPAA-compliant; logs and audit must be separable per customer.
- Timeline: pilot kick on 2028-04-01.

Can you send a short matrix (capex vs opex, SLA diff, procurement path) by EOD Thursday? Rachel from procurement is looped.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Platform | VerityCare

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@veritycare.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: 2028-02-27T13:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: VerityCare pilot hosting options

Hi Tom — appreciate the clear brief, and congrats on getting the pilot live. High-level recommendation below; I attached a short workbook (veritycare_capacity_scenarios.xlsx) and a one-pager (pilot_map_v1.pdf).

Executive summary (short):
- Recommended minimal Dedicated starting slate: 4 x A100/80GB-equivalent GPUs (reserved), configured as a private VPC placement with per-tenant networking. This covers ~15k q/day with room for 2x burst and gives the simplest procurement path (monthly reserved contract).
- Recommended Private (customer-managed on-prem): 3 physical nodes (each 2x A100 equiv) + 1 warm spare (total 7 units equivalent). Higher up-front procurement and longer lead time, but gives maximum data isolation and local KMS control.
- Fallback / burst: enable Redwood Dedicated burst to a regional shared pool with autoscaling rules and automatic downgrade to smaller-quantized model variants if the reserve is exhausted. Fallback plan included in sheet.

Tradeoffs:
- Cost: Dedicated (reserved) amortized is ~30% lower than Private in short-term (12-month) due to Redwood managing utilization; Private becomes cheaper only if VerityCare can fully pack GPUs for other workloads.
- SLA & Ops: Dedicated: 99.9% SLA with integrated monitoring. Private: SLA depends on VerityCare infra + Redwood private control plane (we provide observability & ops runbooks).
- Time to pilot: Dedicated start ~2–3 weeks (contract + VPC peering); Private start ~8–12 weeks (procurement + on-prem setup + network validation).

Key asks from your side to finalize numbers:
1) Typical concurrency distribution (peak qps) — if you can share an hourly heatmap that helps refine sizing.
2) Confirmation on KMS choice (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed).
3) Any regulatory requirements beyond HIPAA (e.g., state-level data residency).

Next steps: I’ll loop infra to produce an alternate set of configurations with H100 vs A100 equivalents (performance per $), and a short rollback ladder. Proposed internal owners: karthik (tiling/throughput), naomi (compliance), aditya (pricing).

—
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example
Attached: veritycare_capacity_scenarios.xlsx, pilot_map_v1.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@veritycare.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.example>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: 2028-02-28T08:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: VerityCare pilot hosting options

Thanks — I dug into the workload shape you described. A few clarifying notes and an optimization play we should consider:

- Workload shape: 15k q/day with 95th 250ms implies modest concurrency but spikes during office hours. If peak qps is < 40, the 4x-A100 dedicated slate is conservative and gives headroom for new routes. If peaks approach 80 qps, we should plan 6 units or add a GPU-backed burst lane.
- Quantization & model mix: If VerityCare is open to int8 or dynamic quantization for the summarization model, we can reduce the dedicated footprint by ~30% while keeping latency targets for short prompts — I flagged this in the workbook under scenario B.
- Autoscale policy: propose steady state 2 units hot, scale to 4 units at queue depth threshold X, and use warm standby for faster spin-up in Dedicated. For Private we suggest 1 warm spare to avoid long recovery windows.
- Observability hooks: we need tenant-level tracing to be enabled for audit. Naomi — can you confirm any special log retention/segregation constraints here?

Action: I’ll prepare two concrete config rows (A100 conservative, quantized-A100 optimized) and a short cost delta.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.example>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@veritycare.com>

Date: 2028-03-01T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing ask: VerityCare pilot hosting options

Tom / team — quick infra notes from our ops side:

- BYOK & KMS: yes, Dedicated VPC placement supports customer KMS integration (we create an external keybinding and do not store key material). See attached kms_flow_diagram.png for reference. Private on-prem can use local HSMs — we have a validated runbook to map key hierarchies.
- Log segregation: Dedicated supports S3 export per-tenant with bucket isolation + IAM roles. We will expose a signed delivery job and retention policy exported to your S3. For Private, logs remain in-customer control.
- Sizing (conservative -> optimized):
  * Dedicated (recommended pilot slate): 4 x A100-80GB equiv (hot) + autoscale to 8 for burst. Expected steady CPU/GPU utilization 40–60% for 15k q/day.
  * Private on-prem baseline: 3 physical servers (2 x A100-equivalents each) + 1 spare = 7 units equivalent. Warm spare avoids cold-start for kernel init and model pulls.
- Network zones: we’ll need two dedicated subnets (control plane and data path) and a separate peering connection. I attached network_zones.drawio.

Operational fallback ladder (short):
1) Dedicated reserved + burst to shared pool (automatic).
2) If burst exhausted, we switch to quantized model variants with weighted routing (lower cost / degraded fidelity).
3) If both fail (extreme case), route reads to cached responses and open a support incident for capacity expansion.

I’ll add the exact cost rows to the workbook; putting this on Marissa to coordinate the pricing ask and on Aditya to create a procurement-friendly quote.

Monica Patel
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attached: network_zones.drawio, kms_flow_diagram.png

- Compliance gate: Naomi will propose retention & audit defaults and a short SOC2+HIPAA checklist for the pilot (target Fri).
- Procurement: Rachel — if you can share the PO template and expected PO date we’ll align the contract timeline.

I’ve scheduled a 30-minute sync next week for final run-through; calendar invite in the HubSpot deal link. Please add the ops person who will own the S3 bucket.

If there are no objections I’ll mark the pilot as "Dedicated-first with Private fallback" in the deal plan (VC-2028-PILOT-47).

Best,
Marissa
